problem: The sentence 'Comparison operators == !=  = produce a Bool' is broken: two operators are missing and '=' (assignment) is shown as producing a Bool. Assignment does not produce a Bool in Swift, and a student will read '=' as a comparison.
fix: Comparison operators == != < > <= >= produce a Bool. The single = is assignment, not comparison.

problem: The switch snippet is followed by '[shown output]' but the code contains no print statement and no declaration of km or rate, so there is nothing to show as output.
fix: Add the declaration and a print, e.g. let km = 12.0; var rate = 0.0; switch km { ... }; print(rate), and show the output 11.5.

problem: 'The word before a parameter is its argument label' is misleading. The full form is func f(label name: Type), so the label is the word before the parameter name, not before the parameter; when only one word is written it acts as both, as with km in fareLabel(km:).
fix: In func f(label name: Type), label is the argument label typed at the call site and name is the parameter name used inside the body. With one word, as in fareLabel(km: Double), that word is both. Write _ in the label position to drop the label.
